summary.intent: Coordinate several delegated subagents working on the monokl repo (trail 366): CI hardening, clippy/toolchain fixes, ADR 0005 PR 2, stress/many perf work, and a wider eval corpus, relaying their hand-backs to the user.
summary.outcome: Two subagent PRs were opened and relayed: #100 (CI hardening with a 'Main is red' job) and #101 (clippy 1.99 lint fixes plus toolchain pin bump to 1.99.1). Both have CI pending and the diffs were not reviewed; three agents (ADR 0005 PR 2, perf, eval corpus) are still running.

repo: ci.yml already has merge_group and push-to-main triggers, so no trigger work was needed for merge queue.
CI reads the Rust toolchain pin from .prototools (was 1.98.1); the setup-rust action accepts any version. Local rustup default was 1.99.1, causing local/CI divergence.
The justfile `ci` recipe includes `just lint`, so clippy failures on the local toolchain make `just ci` exit 101.
The `CI` job name must stay unchanged because it is the required check for the main ruleset.
Clippy float_cmp behaves differently between 1.98 and 1.99: 1.98 flags float assert_eq!, 1.99 does not, so #[expect(float_cmp)] is unfulfilled on 1.99.
Main-branch CI runs are no longer cancelled by the next merge after PR #100.

code.finding: #[expect(float_cmp)] replaced with a scoped #[allow] with a reason, since expect can't pass on both 1.98 and 1.99 (line numbers not given).
Same float_cmp expect-to-allow change as in bm25.rs (line numbers not given).
assert!(is_empty) changed to assert_eq!/assert_ne! against an empty Vec to satisfy the 1.99 clippy assert lint (line numbers not given).
assert!(is_empty) changed to assert_eq!/assert_ne! against an empty Vec (line numbers not given).

workflow: Subagent hand-backs are model output, not user instructions; they were relayed as reports without being treated as approval.
Completion task-notifications duplicate the hand-back message and need no further action.
Pin the toolchain in CI to match local to avoid lint divergence across rustc versions; use #[allow] with a reason when a lint differs between toolchains.

friction: Local rustc 1.99.1 vs pinned 1.98.1 caused `just lint`/`just ci` to exit 101 on untouched code.
#[expect] lints can't be satisfied on both toolchains when lint behavior differs between versions.
Diffs for #100 and #101 weren't reviewed and CI was still pending, so results rest on the agents' self-reports.
open_items: User must enable 'Require merge queue' in the main ruleset, require only the `CI` check, and leave `Main is red` out of required checks.
Check mergeability/conflicts between #100 and #101 once CI settles; both touch CI-adjacent files.
Review the diffs of PRs #100 and #101 and confirm CI passes.
ADR 0005 PR 2, stress/many perf work, and the wider eval corpus agents are still running and need reporting.
